bottleneck: Neuroscience can map correlations between brain activity and experience with increasing precision, yet cannot explain why physical processes are accompanied by subjective experience at all — why seeing red feels like something rather than nothing. This explanatory gap persists across every theory: neural correlates describe, they do not explain, and no experiment has been designed that could distinguish an explanation from a redescription. The problem may be structural, since science is third-person and experience is first-person, with no bridge between the two vocabularies.
current_state: Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, and others compete without consensus or decisive experiments. Christof Koch and others now openly revisit whether materialism can close the gap at all.

title: Hard problem of consciousness resists explanation
why_it_blocks: Every neuroscience of mind rests on an unexplained foundation. Until experience itself is explained, theories of cognition, mental illness, and machine consciousness stand on unexamined ground, and claims about artificial sentience remain untestable.
